name: Appeal to Heaven flag
description: A white field bearing a green pine tree beneath the motto 'AN APPEAL TO HEAVEN'.
history: Flown from October 1775 by the squadron of cruisers George Washington commissioned at the siege of Boston, and later the ensign of the Massachusetts state navy. The white pine was New England's emblem; the motto quotes John Locke's justification of revolution when no earthly authority remains. The flag has seen renewed use in 21st-century American politics.
